So I haven't really seen any detailed rules in the books about crafting health potions. I also haven't seen anything online that I care for either. I have a player interested in crafting them and I don't want him to be able to spam craft. I came up with the following homebrew rules and I'd like to see what you guys think.

Finding Herbs

  1. Proficiency in Nature needed
  2. Add +2 to check if proficient with Herbalism kit [Thanks to /u/sinsaint]
  3. 15 min to find one herb
  4. Nature check to find one herb with a DC 15
  5. The DC changes depending on the environment, but is normally 15
  6. On a failed check, 15 min were wasted
  7. On a success of 10 or more over the DC, two herbs were found
  8. It takes 4 herbs per die
  9. A minimum of 4 herbs are needed regardless of the number of die
  10. In other words, a normal health potion (NHP) (2d4+2) would take 8 herbs (more on the +2 later)

Crafting The Potion

  1. Crafters do not need to be proficient in Arcana to craft
  2. Herbalism kit and proficiency with it is needed [Changed to needing proficiency since I added that the crafter needs Alchemist's Supplies]
  3. -NEW- PC can spend 5g a day for two tendays (total of 100g) to gain training from an alchemical teacher with a Herbalism kit.
  4. -NEW- Artisan's tools (Alchemist's Supplies) needed, but proficiency is not [Only a Dwarf, Monk, Folk Hero, and Guild Artisan can be proficient in using Alchemist's Supplies. This greatly limits who can craft them. I don't like that.]
  5. If crafter is proficient with Alchemist's Supplies, then add +2 to Arcana check
  6. Add Int mod to final potion (That's what replaces the +2 in a NHP)
  7. Arcana check to craft with a DC 17 + (number of attempted dice / 2) [Changed "DC 15" to "DC 17" due to ease of success by Int-based PCs]
  8. On a fail, half of the herbs are destroyed
  9. On a success of 10 or more over the DC, double the Int mod
  10. Average end result will resemble the following formula [(# of herbs / 4) d4 + Int mod]
  11. Max number of dice able to be crafted equals the crafters level divided by 2
  12. No level requirement to craft
  13. In other words, a level 1 crafter can only make a healing potion that is equal to his/her Int mod
  14. A level 1 crafter with a negative Int mod unknowingly creates a poison that deals damage equal to his/her Int mod
  15. Crafting takes (# of attempted die / 2) hour per die [Changed "1 per hour" to "(# of attempted die / 2) per hour" to allow for better scaling]
  16. A minimum of 1 hour is needed regardless of the number of die
  17. In other words, a NHP requires 2 hours to craft
  18. Players can buy recipes from select people at 5x the cost of the potion they're wanting to brew (Use DMG 135 and 188 as reference)
  19. Recipes lower the crafting DC by 5
  20. They would need to find separate ones for potions with different numbers of dice

It might be too simple for some and too complex for others, but I'd like to get everyone's thoughts on its balance, regardless of its subjective level of complexity. I haven't put it into play yet. I've just been doing quick house rules to keep the game going. I was thinking about homebrewing a feat listed below

Medic

  1. Double the number of herbs found on a successful Nature check
  2. 6 herbs can be used, instead of 4, per die and the number of resulting potions will be 2 [Removed since it would allow serious spam crafting]
  3. Crafting a potion of healing takes half the time
  4. +3 to all checks used to find herbs for potions of healing and craft potions of healing

Note: I thought about switching the +3 bonus with a "+1 to Int up to 20", but I thought it might be too OP.

The rules for crafting healing potions are covered on the PHB, page 187.

"You can craft nonmagical objects, including adventuring equipment..."

Potions of healing show up on the "Adventuring Gear" list and in their descriptions. You'll notice though that Greater, Superior, nor Supreme show up on that list, just common potions of healing.

You're right, it does say you can, but it doesn't say how you do it. That's what these rules cover.

You might also need access to special materials or locations necessary to create it. [PHB 187]

That's covered by the "Finding Herbs" rules

For every day of downtime you spend crafting, you can craft one or more items with a total market value not exceeding 5 gp, and you must expend raw materials worth half the total market value. [PHB 187]

That makes crafting potions of healing a ridiculous task seeing how it would take 10 days to create a single potion of healing. The latter part also makes searching for herbs a un-needed task. In turn, it then costs 25g and 10 days to craft a single 2d4+2 potion of healing with no checks

As for crafting the higher strengths, it makes sense to me that someone that's able to craft a regular potion would get better at it over time. That practice would result in stronger potions. Now, you could utilize a XP gain from each potion made, but that makes it significantly more complex than it needs to be.

See, this is the part where'd I'd hand wave it and ask the player (half joking, half serious), "Okay, so now that you know what goes into your effort to create a healing potion, do you truly want to pursue the life of an alchemist, or do you want to continue being an adventurer?

I don't have a problem with players crafting some simple stuff, but when it gets into this level of crafting, then they really need to rethink exactly what it is they're wanting out of that character. You either spend your time adventuring and getting good at your class, or you spend your time becoming a chef or an alchemist or something. Not that there's anything wrong with wanting to be a master chef, but if that's what a character wants to do, it's time for that player to retire that character to pursue that life and start a new character that wants to adventure.

You can create up to three potions at a time; creating a fourth potion causes the oldest currently active one to immediately lose its potency.
